title: Katedrala architecture (strict, schema 1.0.0)
description: A Katedrala architecture document (katedrala analyze). Strict producer schema for exactly this version.

$schema.description: URI of the JSON Schema the document conforms to.

schemaVersion.description: Semantic version of the IR schema (not of Katedrala).

edges.description: Sorted by source, then target, then kind.

entryPoints.description: Sorted by entity, then kind, then source.

ArchitectureDocument.description:
The Katedrala architecture document (`katedrala analyze --format json`).

Determinism: for identical inputs (content, configuration, Katedrala version) every field except `run` is identical, byte for byte when serialized with `serializeDocument`.

adapters.description: Language adapters that processed files, sorted by id.

plugins.description: Plugins that contributed to the result, sorted by id. Omitted when none.

GeneratorInfo.description: The tool that produced a document or report.

ToolVersion.description: Name and version of a tool component (an adapter or a plugin).

id.description: `repo:<normalized remote>` when the repository has an `origin` remote (e.g. `repo:github.com/acme/shop`), otherwise `repo:<name>`.

name.description: Display name: the configured name, else the root package manifest's name, else the last segment of the normalized remote, else `repository`. Never derived from the checkout directory's name, so the same content analyzed from different clones yields the same document.

vcs.description: Version-control metadata, when the analysis root is inside a version-controlled repository.

languages.description: Languages present, sorted by descending line count, then by language id.

remote.description: The `origin` remote, normalized: scheme, credentials and a trailing `.git` removed, `git@host:path` rewritten to `host/path` (e.g. `github.com/acme/shop`).

VcsType.description: Version-control systems. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.

lines.description: Lines in files of this language whose content was read.

analyzedFiles.description: Files parsed by a language adapter (analysis status `parsed` or `partial`).

failedFiles.description: Files whose reading or parsing failed (analysis status `failed`).

lines.description: Lines in files whose content was read.

unresolvedImports.description: Import entries whose specifier could not be resolved (see `diagnostics`).

unresolvedReferences.description: References recorded by adapters that the linker could not bind to a declaration. References an adapter cannot express (e.g. calls on values of unknown type) are not recorded and therefore not counted.

revision.description: The analyzed commit, or the working tree's `HEAD` commit.

subdirectory.description: The analysis root relative to the version-control top-level directory (POSIX, "" when equal). Absent when the root is not inside a repository. Consumers keying caches by commit must include it.

contentDigest.description: `sha256:<hex>` over the listed files: for each file in path order the line `<path>\t<hash or ->\t<size>\n`. Identifies the analyzed content independently of how it was obtained.

analysisDigest.description: `sha256:<hex>` over everything besides content that influences results: the effective Katedrala configuration and options, and the versions of Katedrala, its adapters and plugins. Documents with equal content and analysis digests are identical.

projectConfigurationDigest.description: `sha256:<hex>` over the project configuration files adapters read (e.g. `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`), already part of the content; reported separately to explain resolution changes.

SnapshotKind.description: Kinds of snapshot. `working-tree`: files as they are on disk. `git-revision`: files as committed in a git revision. `in-memory`: files supplied programmatically. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.

subject.description: First line of the commit message.

dirty.description: For working-tree snapshots: whether analyzed files differ from `HEAD`.

symbols.description: Whether `symbols` lists declarations. When false, `symbols` is empty and file `symbols` lists are empty.

relationships.description: `symbol`: code relationships keep symbol endpoints. `file`: symbol endpoints are lifted to their files (and aggregated), so every edge connects files, packages and externals.

DocumentDetail.description: How much detail a document contains. Large repositories may be analyzed at file granularity to keep documents small; consumers use this to distinguish "omitted" from "none".

maxProvenancePerEdge.description: Maximum provenance entries per edge; null means unbounded.

DocumentLimits.description: Bounds applied to lists in the document. Every bounded list documents which bound applies.

name.description: Last path segment; the repository name for the root.

directories.description: Direct child directories, sorted by id.

files.description: Files directly inside this directory, sorted by id.

id.description: `pkg:<ecosystem>:<path>`; stable across renames of the declared name.

name.description: Declared name; for unnamed manifests, the manifest directory path ("." for the root).

path.description: Directory containing the manifest ("" for the analysis root).

private.description: Whether the manifest marks the package as not publishable.

workspaceRoot.description: Whether this manifest declares a workspace (monorepo root).

declaredDependencies.description: Dependencies declared in the manifest, sorted by name, scope, version range, then target.

dependencies.description: Observed code-level dependencies of the package's files on other packages and externals.

dependents.description: Packages whose files depend on this package's files.

PackageEntity.description: A unit declared by a package manifest (e.g. an npm `package.json`).

PackageId.description: `pkg:<ecosystem>:<manifest directory>`, e.g. `pkg:npm:packages/api`; the root manifest is `pkg:npm:`.

versionRange.description: Version range or protocol as declared (e.g. `^1.2.0`, `workspace:*`).

target.description: The workspace package (internal dependency) or external entity the declaration refers to.

DependencyScope.description: Dependency scopes. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.

entity.description: The unit on the other side.

observations.description: Sum of the underlying edges' observations.

runtimeEdgeCount.description: Underlying edges that are not type-only (0 means the dependency vanishes at runtime).

kindCounts.description: Underlying edge count per relationship kind.

examples.description: Representative underlying edges: sorted by descending observations, then id; truncated to `limits.maxExamplesPerDependency`.

AggregatedDependency.description: An aggregated dependency between two units, derived by lifting the relationships between their files (including symbol-level relationships) to the units, using the metrics projection (`metrics.projection`), so that aggregated dependencies agree with unit metrics. In a `dependencies` list `entity` is the depended-upon unit; in a `dependents` list it is the depending unit.

ComponentId.description: `cmp:<path>`; a component rooted at the analysis root is `cmp:`.

ModuleId.description: `mod:<module key>`: the configured name, or the anchor of an inferred module (see docs/IR.md).

EdgeKindCounts.description: Number of relationships per kind; kinds with none are omitted. Keys are serialized sorted.

EdgeId.description: `edge:<16 lowercase hex digits>`, derived from the edge's kind, source and target.

package.description: The package that owns the file (nearest enclosing manifest), if any.

size.description: Size in bytes of the file as stored (before text normalization).

lines.description: Line count of the normalized text, for files whose content was read.

hash.description: `sha256:<hex>` of the normalized text encoded as UTF-8, for files whose content was read. Changes in line endings alone do not change it.

namespaces.description: Package or namespace names the file declares (e.g. Java `package`, C# `namespace`). Omitted when none.

symbols.description: Symbols declared in this file, in source order.

exports.description: Exported names, sorted by name, then `from`, then `typeOnly`.

roles.description: Architectural roles, sorted by role. Omitted when none.

FileRole.description:
Broad purpose of a file. Classification is heuristic (paths, names, manifests) and configurable.
- `source`: production code. `test`: test code. `declaration`: type declarations only (`*.d.ts`).
- `configuration`: tool or build configuration. `script`: build/maintenance scripts.
- `generated`: generated code. `vendored`: third-party code copied into the repository.
- `documentation`, `asset`, `data`, `other`: non-code files.

adapter.description: `<adapter id>@<adapter version>` that processed the file.

syntaxErrors.description: Number of syntax errors reported by the parser.

FileAnalysis.description:
How deeply a file was analyzed. Katedrala never pretends a file was analyzed when it was not.
- `parsed`: parsed without syntax errors. `partial`: parsed with syntax errors; extraction is best-effort.
- `unsupported`: no language adapter handles this file (listed for completeness only).
- `skipped`: deliberately not parsed (size limit, generated/vendored, configuration); see `reason`.
- `failed`: reading or parsing failed; see `reason`.

specifier.description: The specifier exactly as written; for non-literal specifiers, the source text.

mechanism.description: The syntax that expresses the import.

typeOnly.description: True when the import is used only in type positions (e.g. `import type`).

from.description: The innermost declaration containing the import (e.g. a function with a dynamic import).

wildcard.description: The import brings every exported name into scope (`from x import *`, Java `.*`).

global.description: The import applies to every file of its project (C# `global using`).

optional.description: Failure to resolve at runtime is handled (e.g. Python optional imports).

ImportKind.description:
The semantic kind of an import. The syntax used is recorded separately in `mechanism`.
- `static`: a dependency resolved when the importing module loads (ES `import`, CommonJS `require`, TypeScript `import x = require()`, type-only imports, Java/Go/Python imports).
- `dynamic`: loaded on demand (`import()`).
- `re-export`: re-exports another module's names (`export ... from`).
- `side-effect`: loaded only for its side effects (`import "x"`).
- `include`: textual or declaration inclusion (`/// <reference path>`).
- `module-declaration`: declares a child module rather than depending on it (e.g. Rust `mod x;`).

EdgeMechanism.description: The syntactic construct that expresses a relationship. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.

ColumnNumber.description: A 1-based column number in UTF-16 code units.

status.description: Points to one or more files in the document (several for package- or namespace-level imports).

unit.description: The imported unit when it is not a single file (a Go package path, a Java package, a namespace).

status.description: Expected to resolve but did not.
The specifier is not statically known (e.g. `import(variable)`).

ImportResolution.description: Outcome of resolving an import specifier.

ResolutionMethod.description:
How the target of a relationship was determined. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.
- `relative-path`: a relative or absolute path specifier.
- `tsconfig-paths`: a `paths` mapping from a tsconfig. `base-url`: resolved against a tsconfig `baseUrl`.
- `package-imports`: a `#subpath` from the `imports` field of package.json.
- `workspace-package`: a bare specifier naming a package of the same repository.
- `package-self-reference`: a package importing itself by name.
- `external-package`: a bare specifier naming a third-party package.
- `builtin-module`: a platform built-in (e.g. `node:fs`).
- `ambient-module`: a `declare module "x"` declaration.
- `local-declaration`: an identifier bound to a declaration in the same file.
- `import-binding`: an identifier bound by an import, followed to the exporting declaration.
- `namespace-member`: a member access on a namespace import or namespace declaration.
- `re-export-chain`: followed through one or more `export ... from` statements (see `Provenance.via`).
- `global-scope`: an unbound identifier found among global declarations of other files.
- `package-scope`: an unbound identifier found in the same language-level package (e.g. Go, Java).
- `declared-type`: a member access on a value whose declared type names a class or interface.
- `constructor-type`: a member access on a value created with `new` / a constructor.
- `return-type`: a member access on the result of a call whose declared return type is known.
- `inherited-member`: a member found on a base type.
- `manifest`: declared in a package manifest.
- `framework-convention`: established by a framework detector (e.g. dependency injection).

name.description: Exported name; `default` for default exports; `=` for an export assignment (`export =`, `module.exports =`); `*` for `export * from`.

symbols.description: The declarations the name denotes, resolved through re-exports (several when one name denotes both a value and a type, e.g. `const User` and `type User`). Sorted. Omitted when unknown.

from.description: For re-exports: the specifier being re-exported from.

source.description: The producer: a framework detector id (e.g. `nestjs`), `naming`, `location` or `configuration`.

RoleEntry.description: An architectural role with the evidence behind it.

ArchitecturalRole.description: Architectural roles assigned by framework detectors, naming conventions or configuration. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.

Confidence.description: A value in the closed interval [0, 1] expressing how strongly evidence supports a conclusion.

signal.description: Stable kebab-case identifier of the signal, e.g. `internal-dependency-ratio`.

description.description: A complete sentence explaining the observation, e.g. "87% of dependencies stay within the cluster".

value.description: The measured value, when the signal is numeric.

weight.description: The relative weight of this signal in the conclusion, when the conclusion is a weighted aggregate.

entities.description: Entities that exemplify the observation: sorted, and bounded by `limits.maxEvidenceEntities` (selection: sort by id, then truncate).

Evidence.description: One measurable observation supporting a conclusion. Machine-readable (`signal`, `value`) and human-readable (`description`).

EndpointId.description: `endpoint:<16 lowercase hex digits>`, derived from method, path and handler.

name.description: Simple name, e.g. `charge`; `default` for anonymous default exports.

qualifiedName.description: Dot-separated path from the file scope, e.g. `PaymentService.charge`. Within each segment `%`, `.` and `~` are percent-encoded (`%25`, `%2E`, `%7E`), so the dots are unambiguous separators.

parent.description: Lexically enclosing symbol (class of a method, namespace of a function).

owner.description: Semantic owner when it differs from the lexical parent: the type a member belongs to although it is declared elsewhere (Go methods, Rust `impl` blocks, extension methods, module augmentation).

partOf.description: For partial declarations (e.g. C# `partial class`): the canonical declaration.

range.description: The implementation declaration when one exists (e.g. the overload with a body), else the first.

declarations.description: Every merged declaration (overloads, declaration merging), when there is more than one, in source order.

exported.description: Whether the symbol is visible outside its language-level module unit: its file for ECMAScript and Python (exported), its package for Go and Java.

abstract.description: For types: whether the type is abstract in Martin's sense — an interface or trait declaring behaviour (methods), or an abstract class. Data-only interfaces are not abstract.

decorators.description: Decorators / annotations in source order. Omitted when empty.

signature.description: Single-line declaration signature, at most 200 characters.

role.description: The symbol's role when it differs from its file's (e.g. an in-file test module).

roles.description: Architectural roles, sorted by role. Omitted when none.

tags.description: Free-form labels, sorted. Omitted when empty.

SymbolKind.description:
Kind of a declared symbol. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins (which must also give a `SymbolCategory`).
- `module`: a module declaration (`declare module "x" {}`). `namespace`: a namespace / internal module.
- `type-alias`: an alias of another type. `type`: a distinct named type (e.g. Go `type Celsius float64`).
- `field`: a data member; `property`: a data member with accessor semantics (TS class fields are `property`).
- `constant`: an immutable binding whose value is not a function or class.

SymbolCategory.description: A closed, coarse classification of every symbol kind, for consumers that do not know a kind: `type` (declares a type), `callable` (can be invoked), `value` (holds data), `namespace` (groups names).

Range.description: A contiguous region of a source file. `end` is exclusive.

Position.description: A position in a source file.

Visibility.description: Language-neutral visibility, from narrowest to widest: `private` (own declaration), `file`, `protected` (declaration and subtypes), `package` (language-level package, e.g. Java package-private, Go unexported), `module` (compilation unit, e.g. C# `internal`, Rust `pub(crate)`), `public`.

invoked.description: Whether the decorator is invoked (`@Foo()`) rather than referenced (`@Foo`).

arguments.description: Source text of each argument (line endings normalized), each truncated to at most 200 characters.

namespace.description: The identifier namespace (e.g. `npm`, `node`, `pypi`, `env`, `http`). Equal to the second segment of the id. See docs/IR.md for the registry of namespaces.

name.description: Name within the namespace. For packages, the distribution name used by the package manager (the name a manifest declares), not necessarily the name used in imports.

declared.description: For packages: whether every package whose files use this package declares it (in its own manifest or in its workspace root's). `false` indicates at least one undeclared ("phantom") usage.

ExternalKind.description:
Things outside the repository that code depends on. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.
- `package`: a third-party package. `builtin`: a platform built-in module.
- `environment-variable`: configuration read from the environment.
- `service`: a remote service addressed by code, e.g. an HTTP host.
- `datastore`: a database or storage system. `message-channel`: a queue or topic.

id.description: `edge:` + the first 16 hex digits of SHA-256 of `"<kind>\n<source>\n<target>"`. See docs/IR.md.

observations.description: Total number of observations of this relationship (independent of how many are listed).

typeOnly.description: True when every observation is in a type-only position (no use as a value).

confidence.description: Confidence that the relationship exists: the maximum confidence over its observations.

provenance.description: Observations in canonical order (file, line, column, ...), truncated to `limits.maxProvenancePerEdge`. The list is complete if and only if its length equals `observations`.

EdgeKind.description:
Relationship kinds. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins. The listed endpoints are typical; in documents whose `detail.relationships` is `file`, symbol endpoints are lifted to their files.
- `imports`: a file imports a module (file → file | external).
- `re-exports`: a file re-exports from a module (file → file | external).
- `calls`: code invokes a function or method (symbol | file → symbol | external).
- `instantiates`: code creates an instance of a class or struct (symbol | file → symbol | external).
- `extends`: inheritance or embedding (symbol → symbol | external).
- `implements`: a type implements an interface or trait (symbol → symbol | external).
- `references-type`: a type position names a type (symbol | file → symbol | external).
- `uses`: any other value reference, e.g. reading a constant or rendering a JSX component.
- `decorated-by`: a declaration is decorated or annotated by the target (symbol → symbol | external).
- `depends-on-package`: a manifest declares a dependency (package → package | external).
- `reads-configuration`: code reads configuration, e.g. an environment variable (→ external).
- `calls-service`: code calls a remote service, e.g. an HTTP API (→ external).
- `accesses-data`: code accesses a datastore or a persistence model (→ external | symbol).

NodeId.description: Entities that can be the endpoint of a relationship (`EdgeEntity`).

resolution.description: How the target was identified from the construct (the final step when several applied).

confidence.description: Confidence that this particular observation denotes the target.

specifier.description: The module specifier involved, for import-like mechanisms.

typeOnly.description: True when the observation is in a type-only position.

via.description: Re-exporting files traversed between the reference and the declaration, in order.

detector.description: The framework detector that established the relationship, for `framework-convention`.

detail.description: Additional explanation, e.g. the member path that could not be resolved further.

mappedFrom.description: The build output path the entry point was mapped from (e.g. `dist/index.js` → `src/index.ts`).

EntryPointEntry.description: A declared way into the code: manifest entry points, framework conventions, configuration. Used, among others, to avoid reporting entry points as orphans.

EntryPointKind.description:
Kinds of entry point. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.
- `main`, `module`, `exports`, `bin`, `types`: package manifest fields.
- `script`: a manifest script runs the file.
- `framework`: a framework convention (e.g. a Next.js page, a serverless handler).
- `configuration`: declared in Katedrala configuration.
- `convention`: a language convention (e.g. a `main` function).

name.description: Directory name, or package name for package components.

path.description: Directory of the component ("" for the analysis root).

packages.description: Packages declared in this directory or owning it, sorted (usually one).

files.description: Files owned directly by this component (not by a descendant component), sorted.

totals.description: Totals over the whole subtree (this component and all descendants).

modules.description: Modules owning at least one file of the subtree, sorted.

dependencies.description: Dependencies of directly owned files on files directly owned by other components.

dependents.description: Components whose directly owned files depend on this component's directly owned files.

ComponentEntity.description: A physical architectural unit: a package root or a source directory.

id.description: `mod:<configured name>` for declared modules; `mod:<anchor directory>` or `mod:<anchor directory>#<stem>` for inferred modules.

name.description: Display name, e.g. `payments`. Unique among declared modules; inferred names may repeat.

origin.description: `declared` modules come from configuration; `inferred` modules from evidence.

packages.description: Packages owning member files, sorted. Modules may span packages.

files.description: Member files, sorted. Every analyzed source file belongs to at most one module.

components.description: Components owning at least one member file, sorted.

entryPoints.description: Intended public surface: entry files declared in configuration, or barrel/index files at the module's anchor. Sorted.

publicApi.description: Member files that files of other modules import or re-export from (actual usage). Sorted.

ModuleEntity.description: A logical architectural grouping of files.

directory.description: The directory most member files share (see docs/ALGORITHMS.md).

stem.description: The common file-name stem, for modules that cut across directories (e.g. `payment`).

ModuleAnchor.description: What an inferred module's identity and name derive from.

method.description: Identifier and version of the inference method, e.g. `katedrala/module-clustering@1`.

reason.description: One-sentence summary of why the conclusion was reached.

evidence.description: The observations the conclusion is based on, strongest first (ties broken by `signal`).

InferenceInfo.description: Explanation attached to every inferred (as opposed to directly observed) conclusion. Inference is heuristic: `confidence` expresses how strongly the evidence supports the conclusion.

rank.description: Position in the expected dependency order; 0 is the outermost/top layer. Ties are allowed.

LayerEntity.description:
A horizontal architectural role. Layers partition files: a file belongs to at most one layer.

Dependencies are expected to point from a layer to layers of higher `rank` (e.g. `controller` (0) → `service` (1) → `repository` (2)); a dependency toward a lower rank is an "upward" dependency.

method.description: Upper-case method (e.g. `GET`), or `*` when the endpoint accepts every method.

pathComplete.description: False when part of the path (e.g. a router prefix) could not be determined statically.

framework.description: The framework detector that found the endpoint, e.g. `express`.

location.description: Where the endpoint is registered or declared.

EndpointEntity.description: An externally reachable entry into the running system, e.g. an HTTP route.

EndpointProtocol.description: Endpoint protocols. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.

SourceLocation.description: A point in a specific file.

definitions.description: Descriptions of every metric reported, sorted by key.

units.description: Per-unit metrics for packages, modules, layers, components, files and symbols in the projection (symbols only when `detail.symbolMetrics`), sorted by entity id.

edgeKinds.description: Relationship kinds counted as dependencies, sorted.

includeTypeOnly.description: Whether type-only relationships count as dependencies.

fileRoles.description: File roles whose files are nodes of the projection (tests are excluded by default), sorted.

ProjectionInfo.description: The dependency graph projection that metrics and aggregated dependencies were computed on.

key.description: Key as used in `UnitMetrics` (e.g. `instability`) or in `UnitMetrics.extensions` (`<provider>.<name>`).

unit.description: Unit of the raw value, e.g. `count`, `ratio`, `score`.

minimum.description: Lower bound of the value range, when bounded.

maximum.description: Upper bound of the value range, when bounded.

higherIs.description: How to read the value for architectural quality.

levels.description: Levels at which the metric is reported, sorted.

provider.description: `katedrala` or the id of the metric provider plugin.

method.description: Formula identifier and version for composite or approximated metrics, e.g. `katedrala/gravity@1`.

origin.description: Whether the metric is an established measure (with a reference) or a Katedrala heuristic.

MetricDefinition.description: Self-description of one metric, so consumers can present metrics they do not know.

AnalysisLevel.description: Granularity at which a conclusion or a measurement applies. `system` denotes the whole analyzed snapshot.

dependencies.description: Distinct file → file dependencies in the projection.

density.description: `dependencies / (files × (files − 1))`; 0 when there are fewer than two files.

averageFanOut.description: `dependencies / files`; 0 when there are no files.

propagationCost.description: Propagation cost (MacCormack, Rusnak & Baldwin, 2006): density of the transitive-closure ("visibility") matrix including self-visibility; the average share of files a change could reach.

reachabilityExact.description: Whether reachability-based values are exact (false when estimated on very large graphs).

cumulativeComponentDependency.description: Lakos (1996): sum over files of the number of files each depends on transitively, including itself.

averageComponentDependency.description: Lakos (1996): `cumulativeComponentDependency / files`; 0 when there are no files.

normalizedCumulativeComponentDependency.description: Lakos (1996): cumulative component dependency divided by that of a balanced binary tree with the same number of files; values well above 1 indicate tangled dependency structure. 0 when there are no files.

maxDepth.description: Length (in dependencies) of the longest dependency chain in the condensed (acyclic) file graph.

modularity.description: Newman–Girvan modularity of the module partition on the undirected file graph; null when there are no dependencies or no modules.

crossModuleDependencyRatio.description: Share of file dependencies whose endpoints belong to different modules; 0 when there are none.

groups.description: Strongly connected components with more than one unit, or a unit depending on itself.

unitsInCycles.description: Units belonging to such a component.

largestGroup.description: Size of the largest such component.

ratio.description: `unitsInCycles / units`; 0 when there are no units.

CycleSummary.description: Summary of directed cycles (strongly connected components) at one level.

EntropyReport.description: Architectural Entropy (a Katedrala heuristic, not an established metric): a decomposable index of structural disorder in [0, 1]. `score = Σ factors[i].contribution`. See docs/ALGORITHMS.md.

signal.description: Stable kebab-case identifier of the signal, e.g. `reach`.

raw.description: The measurement before normalization, in its natural unit.

normalized.description: The measurement mapped to [0, 1] by a documented, snapshot-independent transform.

weight.description: Weight of the term; the weights of one score sum to 1.

description.description: Short explanation of what the raw value means.

evidence.description: Observations explaining the factor's raw value.

contributions.description: Where the factor comes from: the units contributing most to its raw value, with their share of it (sorted by descending share, then id; bounded). Omitted when the factor is not attributable to units.

size.description: Size of the unit (for components: its directly owned files).

fanIn.description: Distinct units that depend directly on this unit (Martin's afferent coupling, Ca).

fanOut.description: Distinct units this unit depends on directly (Martin's efferent coupling, Ce).

instability.description: Martin's instability `Ce / (Ca + Ce)`; null when the unit has no dependencies and no dependents.

types.description: Types declared in the unit (symbols of category `type`, except type aliases; merged declarations count once).

abstractness.description: Martin's abstractness `abstractTypes / types`; null when `types` is 0.

distance.description: Martin's distance from the main sequence `|A + I − 1|`; null when A or I is null.

transitiveDependents.description: Units that depend on this unit directly or transitively, excluding itself (estimated when not exact).

transitiveDependencies.description: Units this unit depends on directly or transitively, excluding itself (estimated when not exact).

depth.description: Length of the longest dependency chain starting at this unit in the condensed graph (0 for leaves).

betweenness.description: Normalized betweenness centrality (Freeman 1977, computed with Brandes 2001) in [0, 1].

pageRank.description: Relative PageRank on the dependency graph (ComponentRank, Inoue et al. 2005): PageRank × number of units, so the mean is 1 independently of system size.

cohesion.description: For components, modules, layers and packages: share of the dependency weight of member files that stays inside the unit, `internal / (internal + outgoing)`; null when member files have no dependencies. Absent for files and symbols.

cycleGroup.description: The `dependency-cycle` anomaly of the strongly connected component containing the unit, if any.

extensions.description: Measurements contributed by metric plugins, keyed `<provider id>.<metric name>`. Omitted when empty.

UnitMetrics.description: Metrics of one unit in its level's projection.

StructuralRole.description:
Core–periphery role of a unit (Baldwin, MacCormack & Rusnak, 2014), from visibility fan-in (VFI) and visibility fan-out (VFO):
- `core`: high VFI and high VFO (typically members of the largest cyclic group).
- `shared`: high VFI, low VFO — widely used, depends on little.
- `control`: low VFI, high VFO — orchestrates many others.
- `periphery`: low VFI and low VFO. `isolated`: no dependencies and no dependents.

GravityScore.description: Architectural Gravity (a Katedrala heuristic, not an established metric): how structurally important a unit is to the rest of the system. `score = Σ terms[i].contribution`. Method and normalization are described in `MetricsReport.definitions` (key `gravity`) and docs/ALGORITHMS.md.

signal.description: Stable kebab-case identifier of the signal, e.g. `reach`.

raw.description: The measurement before normalization, in its natural unit.

normalized.description: The measurement mapped to [0, 1] by a documented, snapshot-independent transform.

weight.description: Weight of the term; the weights of one score sum to 1.

description.description: Short explanation of what the raw value means.

ScoreTerm.description: One term of a decomposable score (Architectural Gravity, Architectural Entropy, risk scores). `contribution = weight × normalized` and `score = Σ contribution` (after rounding, within 1e-9).

id.description: Directional types: `anomaly:<type>:` + hash of `"<source>\n<target>"`. Other types: hash of the sorted subject ids joined by `"\n"`. See docs/IR.md.

subjects.description: Every entity involved, sorted by id.

source.description: For directional types: the depending unit.

target.description: For directional types: the depended-upon unit.

title.description: Short title, e.g. "Dependency cycle between 3 modules".

evidence.description: Strongest first (ties broken by signal). For cycles, includes representative cycle paths.

confidence.description: How strongly the evidence supports the anomaly.

edges.description: Relationships that constitute the anomaly (e.g. the edges inside a cycle), sorted.

locations.description: Places to look at, sorted, truncated to `limits.maxLocationsPerFinding`.

suggestion.description: A concrete, evidence-based suggestion, when one exists.

AnomalyType.description:
Anomaly types. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins. Directional types (marked →) set `source` and `target`; the others describe a set of `subjects`.
- `dependency-cycle`: one strongly connected component (subjects: its members).
- `god-component`: a unit with outlying size, fan-in and/or fan-out (subjects: the unit).
- `hub`: a unit with outlying centrality (subjects: the unit).
- `boundary-bypass` →: a unit uses another module's internals although the module declares entry points.
- `upward-dependency` →: a dependency against the expected layer direction.
- `unstable-dependency` →: a dependency on a less stable unit (Stable Dependencies Principle).
- `coupled-cluster`: a group of units with outlying mutual dependency density (subjects: the group).
- `orphan`: a unit with no meaningful connectivity that is not a known entry point (subjects: the unit).
- `zone-of-pain`: concrete and stable with many dependents (subjects: the unit).
- `zone-of-uselessness`: abstract and unstable (subjects: the unit).
- `undeclared-dependency` →: a package used by code but not declared by the owning manifest.

Severity.description: Severity shared by diagnostics, anomalies and rule violations. Ordered `info` < `warning` < `error`.

id.description:
`violation:<rule id>:` + hash of `"<rule>
<source>
<target or empty>
<discriminator or empty>"`; the discriminator is a stable identity component (e.g. the cycle's anomaly id), never a measured value.

target.description: The depended-upon unit, for dependency rules.

subjects.description: Every entity involved, for rules about groups (e.g. the members of a forbidden cycle), sorted.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, e.g. "OrderController depends on OrderRepository".

edges.description: Relationships that constitute the violation, sorted.

locations.description: Source locations of the violating relationships, sorted, truncated to `limits.maxLocationsPerFinding`.

RuleViolation.description: A breach of a configured rule. Dependency rules are evaluated on the file-level graph by default and yield one violation per (rule, source file, target file) carrying every underlying edge.

RuleType.description:
Rule types (see docs/RULES.md). Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.
- `forbidden-dependency`: sources must not depend on targets.
- `allowed-dependency`: sources may only depend on the listed targets.
- `layer-order`: dependencies must follow the declared layer order.
- `module-isolation`: a module must not depend on (or be depended on by) other modules.
- `dependency-direction`: dependencies between two groups may only point one way.
- `max-fan-out` / `max-fan-in`: upper bounds on direct dependencies / dependents.
- `no-cycles`: no dependency cycles within the scope.
- `public-api`: other units may only depend on a unit through its declared entry points.

configuration.description: Path of the configuration file the rules came from, relative to the analysis root.

results.description: One entry per configured rule, in configuration order.

digest.description: `sha256:<hex>` of the normalized rule definition; changes when the rule is edited.

violations.description: Number of violations of this rule.

matchedSources.description: Units matched by the rule's source selector (0 usually indicates a misconfigured selector).

matchedTargets.description: Units matched by the rule's target selector, for dependency rules.

problems.description: Configuration problems, e.g. selectors that match nothing. Omitted when none.

RuleResult.description: Outcome of evaluating one configured rule.

RuleProblem.description: A configuration problem detected while evaluating a rule.

RuleProblemCode.description: Codes of rule configuration problems. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.

Diagnostic.description: A problem encountered while analyzing, sorted by file, line, column, code, then message.

DiagnosticCode.description: Diagnostic codes. Values prefixed with `x-` are reserved for plugins.

workers.description: Number of parallel workers used for parsing (1 = in-process).

requestedRevisions.description: Revisions as the user wrote them (e.g. `HEAD~1`), when the run analyzed git revisions.

RunInfo.description: Information about one run that is not determined by the inputs (timings, timestamps, cache usage, the command line). Excluded from determinism guarantees and from serialization unless requested.
